## Verdicts for analysis lines the migrated database cannot settle.
##
## bootstrap_work_file.py classifies most lines mechanically -- an XML record
## from its own text, a field line from a measurement against the migrated
## database. What is left is a DEL field whose column still holds its 19.0
## values, or a NEW one uniform on a populated table: a QUESTION, which only
## reading 20.0's source can answer.
##
## Each verdict below was reached that way and says what was FOUND, not that
## somebody looked. A line with no entry here is written into the work file as
## "# NEEDS A VERDICT", so `grep -c "NEEDS A VERDICT"` counts exactly the debt.
##
## Format: a module:model.field key on its own line, its marker lines, a blank
## line. Lines starting ## are comments and are not part of any marker.

## ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
## 20.0 removes the concept: there is no field anywhere in 20.0 to carry into
## ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

# to carry this into, so there is nothing a script could write

# to carry this into, so there is nothing a script could write

## Handled by a script in this branch

maintenance:maintenance.request.kanban_state
# DONE: post-migration reports it. 20.0 has no value that certainly means 19.0's
# 'blocked' -- blocked says the work cannot proceed where 'changes_requested'
# says a reviewer asked for something -- so the count is reported and the column
# is left where an administrator can act on it

maintenance:maintenance.request.user_id
# DONE: post-migration carries it into user_ids. 20.0's _compute_user_ids adds
# only the equipment's technician, so an assignee who is anyone else is lost --
# which this seed cannot show, because every request is assigned to exactly its
# equipment's technician

maintenance:maintenance.stage.done
# DONE: post-migration reads it. 19.0 recorded completion HERE, on the stage;
# 20.0 records it on maintenance.request.state, and no DEL/NEW pairing on one
# model could have reached across to see that
